alt.en: A pale, jointed bone hook lies horizontally on a grey background; its pointed barb bends down at the right.
alt.zh: 浅色拼接骨钩横置于灰色背景，右端尖锐倒钩向下弯曲。

caption.en: Final Jōmon bone fish hook, about 1000–300 BCE; Met 1975.268.358a, b.

interpretation.en: The hook makes fishing technology visible. Its collection record gives Japan, not a proven findspot at one of the northern World Heritage sites.
interpretation.zh: 鱼钩呈现具体捕鱼技术。馆录仅标注日本，并未确认它出土于北部某处世界遗产遗址。

alt.en: A monochrome photograph shows a cylindrical pottery granary with a broad conical roof and three short feet.
alt.zh: 黑白照片中，圆筒形陶粮仓有宽阔锥形屋顶和三只短足。

caption.en: Eastern Han granary model, first–early third century CE; green lead-glazed earthenware, Met 13.100.11. Monochrome collection photograph.
caption.zh: 东汉粮仓模型，公元一至三世纪初；铅绿釉陶，大都会13.100.11。馆藏黑白照片。

interpretation.en: Models of farm buildings accompanied Eastern Han burials as provisions for the afterlife. The model preserves an imagined household resource, not a measured plan of an imperial granary.
interpretation.zh: 东汉墓葬常放置农用建筑模型，供死后生活所需。模型保存的是来世家产想象，而非帝国粮仓的测绘图。

note.en: The official object page marks the image Public Domain; its saved API record confirms isPublicDomain=true.
note.zh: 官方单件页面标记图像为公共领域，保存的API记录确认isPublicDomain=true。

alt.en: A monochrome photograph shows a two-humped ceramic camel standing with its long neck raised and mouth open.
alt.zh: 黑白照片中，双峰陶骆驼站立，长颈昂起，嘴部张开。

caption.en: Tang tomb figure of a camel, eighth century; sancai-glazed earthenware, Met 67.43.1. Monochrome collection photograph.
caption.zh: 唐代骆驼明器，八世纪；三彩釉陶，大都会67.43.1。馆藏黑白照片。

interpretation.en: This is a ceramic tomb figure, not a picture of a particular caravan. Its two humps and raised neck show how an animal associated with overland travel became a crafted funerary image.
interpretation.zh: 这是陶制明器，不是某支商队的图像记录。双峰与昂颈造型显示，与陆路旅行相关的动物如何成为工匠塑造的随葬形象。

note.en: The official object page marks the image Public Domain; its saved API record confirms isPublicDomain=true.
note.zh: 官方单件页面标记图像为公共领域，保存的API记录确认isPublicDomain=true。

alt.en: A standing crowned figure wears layered necklaces and long drapery above a lotus pedestal; parts of the arms are missing.
alt.zh: 立像戴冠，佩多层璎珞，长衣垂至莲座上方，双臂部分残缺。

caption.en: Limestone bodhisattva with pigment traces, late sixth century, Sui dynasty; probably Guanyin, Met 42.25.3a, b.
caption.zh: 隋代石灰岩菩萨像，六世纪末，存彩绘痕迹；可能为观音，大都会42.25.3a, b。

interpretation.en: The 1.85-metre sculpture adds religious craft to a political chronology. Its identification as Guanyin is probable, not certain; the catalog does not name an imperial patron.
interpretation.zh: 高约1.85米的雕像为政治年表补入宗教工艺。观音身份只是可能的判断，馆录并未指明皇室施主。

note.en: The official object page marks the image Public Domain; its saved API record confirms isPublicDomain=true.
note.zh: 官方单件页面标记图像为公共领域，保存的API记录确认isPublicDomain=true。

title.en: A face carved in Liangzhu jade

alt.en: A rounded, flattened grey-and-brown jade ornament bears two outlined eyes, a short nose and a horizontal mouth.
alt.zh: 扁平圆顶的灰褐色玉饰刻有双眼、短鼻与横向嘴部。

caption.en: Liangzhu-culture nephrite ornament with mask, middle third millennium BCE; Met 18.63.
caption.zh: 良渚文化兽面纹软玉饰，公元前三千纪中期；大都会18.63。

interpretation.en: The museum attributes this carved ornament to Liangzhu culture. It is not documented as a find from the city’s mapped archaeological area, and the face alone cannot identify a named deity.
interpretation.zh: 馆方将此雕刻玉饰归于良渚文化，但未确认它出土于地图所指古城遗址，仅凭面纹也无法辨认某位有名神祇。

note.zh: 官方单件页面标记图像为公共领域，保存的API记录确认isPublicDomain=true。

title.en: Two halves make a moon jar

alt.en: A softly asymmetric white porcelain jar has a round body, short open neck, narrow foot and faint peach-coloured patches.
alt.zh: 白瓷罐圆腹略不对称，短口、窄足，釉面有淡桃色斑。

caption.en: Joseon porcelain moon jar, second half of the eighteenth century; Met 1979.413.1.
caption.zh: 朝鲜王朝白瓷月亮罐，十八世纪后半叶；大都会1979.413.1。

interpretation.en: Potters joined two hemispheres to make these jars. Firing left variations in outline and colour; the poetic name “moon jar” reflects twentieth-century rediscovery of earlier utilitarian vessels.
interpretation.zh: 陶工将两个半球接合成罐，烧制带来轮廓与釉色差异。“月亮罐”这一诗意名称来自二十世纪对早期日用器物的重新发现。
